function.name: read_file
function.description: Returns one page of one existing file as JSON. The page starts at line `offset` (1-based), `column` bytes into that line, and holds up to `limit` lines; a long line continues on the next page. The file's text is in `content` (null for bytes that are not text, with their count in `binary`; a smaller `limit` may isolate them). To continue, call again with `next.line` as `offset` and `next.column` as `column`; `eof` is true at the end of the file, and `changed` is true when the file changed since your last page of it, so read it again from the start. One file per call. No globs, no directories, no recursion. May be refused.

path.description: Absolute path to the file to read.

column.description: Byte offset into the first line, from a previous page's next.column. Default 0.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Replaces the entire contents of path with content. This is not an edit, patch, or append — whatever was there is gone. Read the file before replacing it, every page until `eof` is true if you need all of its contents. Returns one of: applied; not written — nothing was written because the file exists and you have not read it, or it changed since you read it: read it, then write again; unavailable — do not retry; or outcome unknown — the write may have happened: do not retry it. The call's arguments, as JSON with `content` escaped, may be at most 61440 bytes, and a longer call is not run: you get an error giving its size, and the other calls in the reply still run. A large write, even within that limit, must be the only call in its reply; otherwise the reply may be refused, nothing in it is written, and the task ends.

path.description: Absolute path to the file to replace.

content.description: The complete new contents of the file.

function.name: list_directory
function.description: Lists one directory: one name per line, in byte order, each name a JSON string, with `/` after a directory's closing quote. At most 1024 names per call; if there are more, the last line is `truncated — continue with after: "<name>"`, and calling again with that name as `after` returns the next page. Entries you may not see are simply absent, exactly as if they did not exist, and the result has no count or total of anything. An empty result means there is nothing here you may see. Not recursive. May be refused: unavailable — do not retry.

path.description: Absolute path to the directory to list.

after.description: Return only names after this one: the name from the previous page's truncated line.

function.name: stat_path
function.description: Returns what is at one path as JSON: `kind` (file, directory, symlink or other), `size` in bytes, and `mtime_secs`, the last modification in seconds since the Unix epoch. A symlink is reported as itself and is not followed. Nothing else about the path is returned. May be refused: unavailable — do not retry.
